passages.text: In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The digital revolution, for all its emancipatory promise, has spawned a (1)________ of misinformation that threatens the very foundations of informed discourse. Algorithms engineered to maximise engagement tend to privilege sensational content over sober analysis, thereby creating echo chambers in which pre- existing prejudices are relentlessly reinforced. Falsehoods, often cloaked in a veneer of authority, propagate with a speed that verified facts can seldom match. What makes this phenomenon particularly (2)________ is its subtlety. Unlike overt propaganda, which audiences can readily identify and resist, modern disinformation masquerades as ordinary opinion, insinuating itself into conversations with deceptive ease. Even discerning readers occasionally find themselves unwittingly sharing claims that later prove to be entirely (3)________. Regulators face a formidable dilemma. Heavy-handed censorship risks (4)________ the freedom of expression that democratic societies hold sacrosanct, whereas excessive leniency allows pernicious narratives to flourish unchecked. Technology companies, for their part, have been accused of equivocating, professing a commitment to truth while profiting handsomely from the very outrage they claim to deplore. A durable solution, experts contend, must be multifaceted. Media literacy should be embedded in school curricula, enabling young citizens to scrutinise sources and detect manipulation. Simultaneously, platforms must be held accountable for the opaque architecture of their algorithms. Ultimately, however, the (5)________ of truth rests with each individual, for no regulatory framework can wholly substitute for a sceptical and inquisitive mind.
